artifacts.name: About this indicator
artifacts.summary: Maps pedestrian traffic signals that provide acoustic guidance to help blind and partially sighted people cross safely. Like tactile paving, it is best read as a coverage indicator over signalised crossings.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Acoustic pedestrian signals explorer
artifacts.summary: The actual OpenStreetMap objects behind the acoustic pedestrian signals, with their attributes. Zoom in to inspect them.
artifacts.description:
The true OpenStreetMap geometry of every counted feature — points, ways and areas — carrying its name and (where mapped) opening hours. It appears from a neighbourhood zoom level so you can inspect the individual objects rather than an aggregate.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = 0.10. 4 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of acoustic pedestrian signals density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 21 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over acoustic pedestrian signals density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Top sub-areas
artifacts.summary: The 10 best-served neighbourhoods by acoustic pedestrian signals density (per km²). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do acoustic pedestrian signals track where people live? Acoustic pedestrian signals per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its acoustic pedestrian signals per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita
artifacts.summary: Acoustic pedestrian signals per 1,000 residents across the sub-areas — provision relative to need. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of acoustic pedestrian signals per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Coverage on foot
artifacts.summary: About 60% of the area is within 300 m on foot of a acoustic pedestrian signal. About 84% of residents are within reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The area of interest split into the part within reach (on foot) of any feature and the part beyond it. Reachability is computed using straight-line distance.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Underserved areas
artifacts.summary: Share of each neighbourhood beyond 300 m on foot of any acoustic pedestrian signal. About 7,965 residents live beyond that reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by the fraction of its area that lies **beyond reach** (on foot) of any feature — the complement of the coverage map. Darker = more underserved. Use it to target where new provision would reach the most currently-unserved people.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.description:

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Acoustic pedestrian signals heatmap
artifacts.summary: A gridded density of acoustic pedestrian signals across the area — brighter means more. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area of interest, each cell shaded by how many acoustic pedestrian signals fall within it. It reveals clusters and gaps that individual points can hide.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Acoustic pedestrian signals density surface
artifacts.summary: A smoothed, continuous density surface of acoustic pedestrian signals (kernel-style). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of acoustic pedestrian signals: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest acoustic pedestrian signal
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest acoustic pedestrian signal from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest acoustic pedestrian signal. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness
artifacts.summary: How recently each acoustic pedestrian signal was last edited in OpenStreetMap (median 2 yr ago). Darker = longer since the last edit. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: audible_traffic_signals · reachability: straight-line distance.
